title: Feature flag exposure + rollout cohortization for Console usage analytics
creator: Marco Rivera
description:
Background: Product wants to measure feature flag exposure and correlate rollout cohorts with Console adoption, latency, and per-route cost. Currently we only have coarse workspace-level events which make it hard to analyze phased rollouts (canary -> gradual -> global) or to attribute changes in usage to rollout segments. This ticket proposes a curated set of warehouse tables and ingestion changes to create deterministic cohort keys for rollouts and an optimized factset for joining exposures to route-level activity.

Goals:
- Produce a curated table `ww_rollout_exposures` (name tentative) keyed by (workspace_id, rollout_id, cohort_key, exposure_timestamp) that captures deterministic cohort assignment and the exposure context (flag metadata, percentage target, rollout stage).
- Build a companion daily-timeseries materialized table `ww_rollout_cohort_daily` with pre-aggregated metrics (active_routes, avg_latency_p50/p95, token_count, invocation_count, error_rate, cost_estimate) partitioned by date and cohort_key for fast dashboarding.
- Ensure join-friendly schemas (small pk types, surrogate cohort_key string) and SCD-safe lookup tables for rollout metadata.
- Keep storage + query cost under target: incremental model builds, partition pruning, and confine wide scans to backfills.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Deterministic cohort assignment: use a hash(workspace_id || rollout_id || salt) mod 10000 to assign stable bucket ids, then map to named cohorts (canary, 10pct, 50pct, etc.). Pro: stable across reingestion; Con: requires careful salt/versioning when rollout strategy changes.
- Materialization cadence: daily materialized table with incremental dbt models. Real-time streaming would be ideal but is higher infra cost and higher cardinality; we will surface near-RT checks via Kinesis/Dataplane counters but rely on daily aggregates for analytics.
- Storage: implement as clustered partitioned BigQuery partitioned by dt and clustered on cohort_key + workspace_id (or equivalent settings in Redshift if customer env).

Schema proposals (high level):
- lookup_rollouts (SCD2-like): rollout_id, flag_key, created_at, retired_at, rollout_strategy_json, version_tag
- ww_rollout_exposures (event-fact): exposure_id, workspace_id, rollout_id, cohort_key, assigned_bucket, exposure_timestamp, source_event_id, properties_json
- ww_rollout_cohort_daily (agg): dt, cohort_key, rollout_id, workspace_count, route_count, invocations, tokens, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, errors, est_cost_usd

Backfill plan and lineage:
- Backfill exposures for the past 90 days using existing event store (event_stream_extracted). Backfill job will be split by date ranges and run with smaller worker pools to avoid cluster contention.
- dbt models will include explicit upstream dependencies and tags. Update the docs/lineage in Confluence and register models in the Console analytics workspace.

Implementation notes and current progress:
- Schema review completed 2025-02-18; notes in the design doc (see related_docs).
- Prototype extraction SQL produced; initial performance test on a 7-day slice showed 25% slower joins due to high cardinality `properties_json`. Mitigation: extract only required properties into columns (flag_key, rollout_id, event_source) and keep properties_json as TEXT for rare ad-hoc use.
- dbt models: `ep_rollout_lookup` (bronze -> silver) and `f_rollout_exposures` implemented as draft in branch feature/rollout-cohorts. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/warehouse/pull/2345 (see related_prs).
- Materialized view `mv_rollout_cohort_daily` created in dev; nightly run scheduled in Airflow DAG `console_analytics_rollouts_v2`.

Open risks / blockers:
- Need confirmation on primary key sizing for exposures table (64-bit vs UUID). Larger keys increase storage; UUID preferred for cross-service correlation. Action: engineering to align with infra (ticket ENG-90110).
- RBAC: the exposures table contains workspace-level info; confirm that row-level security policies are compatible with Console's analytics role scopes. Security review requested if we widen access.

Next steps (short-term):
- Finish PR review and merge dbt models (owner: Ayesha) — target 2025-03-08.
- Run controlled backfill (past 30 days) to validate aggregation correctness and performance — target 2025-03-15.
- Add dashboard panels and alerting for cohort anomalies (sudden drop in invocations or spike in latency) — owner: Analytics PM.

Success metrics:
- Ability to answer: "What percent of routes in cohort X saw >10% latency increase within 7 days of exposure?" in < 30s on the dashboard.
- Backfills complete within SLA (30 days historical backfill completes within 48 hours window per 7-day chunk).
- Dashboard adoption: product + growth use these cohort breakdowns for at least 3 rollouts in H1 2025.
